_about: Categories A and C are EDUCATIONAL RECOMMENDATIONS written by Claude (AI) from general medical knowledge and the NEET-PG syllabus areas; they are not derived from exam counts. Category B is computed by analyze.py from observations.json and is not listed here. Nothing here is a probability of appearance.

A.name: Acid-base and electrolyte disorders
A.rationale: Underpins nephrology, critical care, endocrinology and toxicology; the same reasoning (anion gap, compensation, sodium/potassium algorithms) recurs across subjects and question formats.

A.name: Shock, resuscitation and trauma assessment
A.rationale: Primary survey, GCS and shock physiology link surgery, anaesthesia and medicine; two related concepts appear in this dataset (NEET-PG 2025, INI-CET May 2026).

A.name: Antimicrobial choice, toxicity and resistance
A.rationale: Drug-bug matching and signature toxicities connect pharmacology, microbiology and clinical medicine.

A.name: Cell injury, inflammation and neoplasia (including translocations)
A.rationale: General pathology is the base for systemic pathology and haematology; two translocation concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A.name: Autonomic pharmacology and toxidromes
A.rationale: Receptor pharmacology explains drug effects, poisoning syndromes and perioperative care.

A.name: ECG and arrhythmias
A.rationale: Physiology of conduction to bedside ECG diagnosis and management; image-based in many formats.

A.name: Screening tests, biases and study designs
A.rationale: Needed to read any evidence and frequently calculation-based; two related concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A.name: Obstetric emergencies (PPH, eclampsia, shoulder dystocia, cord prolapse)
A.rationale: Time-critical algorithms with high clinical stakes; four related concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A.name: HIV and tuberculosis
A.rationale: Spans microbiology, pharmacology, medicine and national programmes; two related concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A.name: Endocrine emergencies (DKA, adrenal crisis)
A.rationale: Physiology-driven management with clear algorithms; adrenal insufficiency appears in the 2025 recall list.

C.name: Sepsis and septic shock: recognition and first-hour care
C.rationale: High clinical importance; no observation in this dataset, which says more about the dataset's size than about the exam.

C.name: Anaphylaxis
C.rationale: Life-threatening emergency with a single first-line drug and dose; not observed in this dataset.

C.name: Acute ischaemic stroke: thrombolysis eligibility and time windows
C.rationale: Guideline-dependent and clinically critical; not observed in this dataset.

C.name: Neonatal resuscitation and newborn care
C.rationale: Algorithmic and important; appears only as a coaching forecast (S03), not as an observation.

C.name: Medical ethics, consent and the 2024 criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA)
C.rationale: India's criminal laws changed on 1 July 2024, so older section numbers in books are outdated; syllabus relevance is high and historical data cannot reflect it yet.

C.name: Snakebite and common poisonings
C.rationale: Common in India with specific antidotes and protocols; not observed in this dataset.

C.name: National health programme updates (e.g. TB elimination, NCD screening)
C.rationale: Programmes change often; current versions matter more than historical frequency.

C.name: Video-assessable clinical skills (gait, movement disorders, examination signs)
C.rationale: FMGE introduced video questions in June 2026 (S12). No NEET-PG video questions are reported, so this is a hypothesis about format spread, not a finding.

revision_note: Expanding-interval review (a common spaced-repetition schedule). The app adapts it per question from your answers.
